Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

density noun

also denseness, thickness (density), compactness, population density, dense

classical

Plin. NH 35.178: in dēnsitātem coit (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 13.78: chartae (Lewis & Short)

dēnsitās, dēnsitātis f.

noun, third declension

density, thickness, compactness

Pliny’s word, of mud, paper, liquids; Quintilian uses it of a closely packed style (sententiārum, Quint. 8.5.26). Not before Augustus (Lewis & Short). The modern word for density in physics.

Other words

  • crassitūdō, crassitūdinis f. — thickness, density

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. B.C. 2.8: parietum (Lewis & Short); Cic. Div. 1.93: āëris (Lewis & Short)

    Chiefly thickness, of walls, posts, wax and honey; of the air, its density.

  • frequentia, frequentiae f. — crowding, a great number of people in a place

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.2.189: summa hominum (Lewis & Short)

    For a crowded place or a dense population: frequentia hominum; the adjective is frequēns, crowded.

  • spissitās, spissitātis f. — compactness, density

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Vitr. 2.9 (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 18.304 (Lewis & Short)

    Post-Augustan and very rare (Lewis & Short).

See also thick.
